WHY DOES THIS FISH LOOK LIKE IT HAS NO FACE? 

Scientists just filmed one of the strangest fish on Earth more than 16,000 feet beneath the Pacific Ocean.

It looks completely faceless.

But the truth is even stranger.

The faceless cusk eel actually has tiny eyes buried beneath its skin, while its mouth sits unusually low on its head.

At that depth, there is almost no sunlight—and the animal appears to rely heavily on smell and touch to navigate.

This footage comes from the current 2026 E/V Nautilus deep-sea expedition.

🌊 Would you recognize this as a fish if you saw it in the dark?

#DeepSeaMystery #OceanDiscovery #FacelessFish #PacificOcean #MarineScience

CAN INVISIBLE RADON REVEAL HIDDEN MINERALS? 

Scientists are testing a strange new clue in the deep Pacific.

During a NOAA expedition near American Samoa, researchers are collecting seawater directly above the abyssal seafloor and measuring naturally occurring radon.

Why?

Because radon escaping from sediments could act as a geochemical tracer, potentially helping scientists identify areas where valuable deep-sea minerals may be concentrated.

No drilling.

No giant machines digging through the seafloor.

Just an invisible radioactive gas that may reveal what is hiding below.

🌊 Could the ocean itself be giving scientists clues about what lies underneath?
